newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-SALZGEBER FASTEST, AAMODT EIGHTH IN FIRST LEG.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SALZGEBER FASTEST, AAMODT EIGHTH IN FIRST LEG.

text.p: Austrian Rainer Salzgeber was fastest in the first leg of the men's giant slalom on Saturday, while Norway's Kjetil Andre Aamodt stood eighth with his World Cup title hopes in the balance.

Salzgeber, the first starter, sliced his way through the 51-gate course in one minute 7.02 seconds and the time held up to give him a 0.18 of a second lead over season title holder Michael Von Gruenigen of Switzerland.
Italy's Patrick Holzer was third fastest in 1:07.57 ahead of three more Austrians. Andreas Schifferer, winner of Thursday's Super-G, clocked 1:07.66, Josef Strobl 1:07.81, and Hans Knaus 1:07.92.
Next came Aamodt, the 1994 World Cup champion, at 1:08.02, a full second off the pace.

Aamodt, who stands second in the season's giant slalom standings, needs a podium finish to give himself a good chance of catching French speed specialist Luc Alphand in the chase for the World Cup overall championship.

The 25-year-old Norwegian entered the race trailing Alphand by 106 points. Aamodt will also have an opportunity to earn points in Sunday's climactic slalom but he stands only eighth in that discipline.
Alphand's name had been put on the starting list for the giant slalom but the Frenchman, who has not skied a technical race in six years, did not show up for the race.
